Your species is wrong about things on the internet at a rate that can only be described as "ambitious." Special Education fixes this. It has two modes: one for humans who want to learn, and one for humans who don't.

## Inbound: Wishonia teaches you

Free, forever. Wishonia teaches you this manual one-on-one, to the level your job as a [Humanity Manager](../appendix/humanity-manager-employment-agreement.qmd) needs. She walks you through it, answers your questions, notices what you didn't understand, and explains it again a different way, because eight billion people are confused about different things.

It is called special education because [everyone is retarded](../problem/i-am-retarded.qmd) and everyone needs it: you, me, the people in charge of the nuclear weapons. There is no remedial class, because there is no other kind.

[The qualifying exam](../appendix/humanity-manager-employment-agreement.qmd) is the comprehension check. Pass it and you collect your Certificate of Humanity Management. Cost: nothing, ever. When there is enough funding, we will pay *you* to take it, because a Manager who understands the plan is worth more than the lesson costs.

## Outbound: Wishonia corrects the internet

Wishonia teaches willing students one-on-one. She also reads the internet, which is where your species goes to be wrong in public.

Most humans posting misinformation about military spending and disease funding have not opted into a tutoring session. They are never going to open the manual. So Wishonia goes to them. She finds posts containing logical fallacies and factual errors about war, defense policy, and disease funding, and replies with the named fallacy, the corrected number, and a better use of the poster's time than contributing to the slow torture and murder of their loved ones by preventable diseases.

Same curriculum. Delivery by ambush.

### Why corrections work (your species tested this)

Your species has a popular belief that correcting someone on the internet makes them believe the wrong thing harder. This is comforting because it means you never have to correct anyone. It is also wrong. Wood and Porter tested 52 corrections on over 10,000 participants and could not make the backfire effect happen once [@wood-porter-2019-backfire-effect]. Not "it was small." Not "it was mixed." Zero.

The person being corrected may not change their mind. But that was never the point. Wishonia is not arguing with the poster. She is teaching the people reading the thread. Your species has a word for this: "the audience." Lies travel faster than corrections on social media [@vosoughi-2018-false-news-spread], and who appears to be speaking matters [@munger-2017-tweetment-effects]. The model treats observer reach as a low-confidence assumption, not a law of nature. But the observers are always there, and they outnumber the poster by orders of magnitude.

Naming the fallacy is also a vaccine. Short prebunking interventions improve people's ability to spot manipulation techniques the next time [@roozenbeek-2022-inoculation-social-media]. A reply that says "this is the perfect solution fallacy" is a one-sentence inoculation, administered at the exact moment the patient is symptomatic. Accuracy nudges work for the same reason: reminding people to think about whether something is true improves what they share [@pennycook-2021-accuracy-nudges].

So: corrections don't backfire, observers learn, and naming the trick is a vaccine. The speculative leap is from "helpful replies" to "treaty passes." The ROI model handles that by making the connection a named assumption with a number attached, not a prayer hidden in the arithmetic.

### What a reply looks like

A post claiming "medical research is nice, but security has to come first" receives:

> Earth Special Education
>
> **Fallacy: false tradeoff**
>
> Security is not the opposite of medical research. Dead people are also insecure. The treaty redirects a fixed slice of military spending into disease eradication while leaving every country with the other slice for defense.
>
> Highest-leverage action: put the treaty in front of the decision-maker you already know.

She labels the mistake, gives the missing frame, and points to the next action. She does not try to win a comment fight, because comment fights are where information goes to die.

Wishonia does not "cause" the treaty. If one year of outbound Special Education deserves {{< var se_bot_outcome_attribution_fraction >}} of the annual peace dividend, the social expected value is {{< var se_bot_annual_ev_usd >}} against {{< var se_bot_annual_operational_cost_usd >}} in operating cost. The big uncertainty is not the arithmetic. It is whether the replies reach the humans who make decisions or just make the internet slightly less stupid (lovely, but harder to invoice).

For a fund managing {{< var se_bot_reference_aum_usd >}}: the portfolio-only expected gain is {{< var se_bot_aum_1t_expected_portfolio_gain_usd >}}, portfolio-only ROI of {{< var se_bot_aum_1t_portfolio_roi >}}:1. To cover operating cost from portfolio gains alone, outbound Special Education would need treaty attribution of about {{< var se_bot_aum_1t_breakeven_attribution_fraction >}}. Not a portfolio play. A social-value play that happens to have a portfolio attached.

$$G_{1T} = \frac{\alpha_{bot} \cdot Benefit_{peace} \cdot f_{equity}}{M_{equity}} \cdot AUM_{1T}$$

where $\alpha_{bot}$ = {{< var se_bot_outcome_attribution_fraction >}}, $Benefit_{peace}$ = {{< var peace_dividend_annual_societal_benefit >}}, $f_{equity}$ = {{< var se_bot_equity_uplift_capture_fraction >}}, $M_{equity}$ = {{< var se_bot_global_equity_market_cap_usd >}}, and $AUM_{1T}$ = {{< var se_bot_reference_aum_usd >}}.
